simple.meaning: זָמַן (zâman) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to fix (a time).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Ezra, Nehemiah, beginning at Ezra 10:14. The surrounding contexts include offering, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זָמַן (H2163) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: זָמַן (zâman) / H2163 is traced through Ezra 10:14, Nehemiah 10:35, Nehemiah 13:31 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2163. zaman [ זָמַן ] verb (Aramaic and late) only Pu`al Participle be fixed, appointed , of time (Arabic continue , Aramaic Pa`el זַמֵּן , summon to fixed time or place, invite, appoint ; compare זִמָ֑ן below) — מְזֻמָּנִים עִתִּים Ezra 10:14 ; Neh 10:35 ; ׳ע מְזֻמָּנוֺת 13:31 .

occurrences.englishText: Now let our princes be appointed for all the assembly, and let all those who are in our cities who have married foreign women come at appointed times, and with them the elders of every city, and its judges, until the fierce wrath of our God is turned from us, until this matter is resolved.”
and to bring the first fruits of our ground, and the first fruits of all fruit of all kinds of trees, year by year, to Yahweh’s house;
and for the wood offering, at times appointed, and for the first fruits. Remember me, my God, for good.
